clue.text: Drop by and I will put an end to suspense

parts.note: by means past, as in walking by or past
I will contracts to I'll, written without the apostrophe

indicators.note: the end of the word suspense supplies its final letter only

explanation.surface: A speaker promises to drop in and resolve the tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop' looks like a verb but is a noun, a small sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastille is a small lozenge or sweet, also called a drop, as in a cough drop.

clue.text: Features in letter to the king

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Zog was king of Albania

explanation.surface: Something appearing in a letter written to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Zog was king of Albania from 1928 to 1939, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: Phizog is old slang for a face, the features.

clue.text: Thereafter fuel went under a different name

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece goes beneath the first

parts.note: so, as in and so, means thereafter
a briquet is a block of compressed coal dust used as fuel

explanation.surface: After that, the fuel was sold under another brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went under' places BRIQUET below SO in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A sobriquet is a nickname, an alternative name for someone.

clue.text: One periodical that's dropped its centre picture

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: the middle letters of the periodical's word are taken away

parts.note: a magazine is a periodical publication

explanation.surface: A magazine issue that left out its centrefold photo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's dropped its centre' removes AZ, the middle two letters of MAGAZINE.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to picture something in the mind.

clue.text: Compare Liberal president with Nationalist leader

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Weighing a Liberal president against a nationalist head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: To liken one thing to another is to draw a comparison between them.

clue.text: When someone's speaking you interrupt — so do I — that's naughty and offensive

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into, so one piece goes into the middle of the other
the words so do I behave badly and are rearranged
spoken aloud, the word you sounds like the letter U

parts.note: the word you, said aloud, is the letter U

explanation.surface: A tirade about interruptions in conversation, admitting to the same bad habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges SO DO I into ODIOS; 'interrupt' puts U inside, after ODIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Something odious is hateful and repugnant, much the same as offensive.

clue.text: Elderly lady always making the same bet

parts.note: do, short for ditto, means the same
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: An old woman who always places the same flutter.
explanation.walkthrough: DO (ditto) is the shorthand for repeating the item above.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, typically an older woman.

clue.text: Author who was bilingual? Yes

parts.note: oui is French for yes
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: Asking whether a writer spoke two languages, and answering yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bilingual' hints that yes is given in two languages. Ouida was a Victorian novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouida was the pen name of Maria Louise Ramé, a popular 19th-century novelist.

clue.text: Leave pond wet, shivering, after drastically curtailed swim

indicators.note: the anagram comes after the letter
cut short severely, so only the first letter of swim survives
shivering means trembling, so the letters of pond wet are shaken up

explanation.surface: A cold swimmer climbing out of a pond after a brief dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shivering' rearranges POND WET to TEPDOWN, after S.
explanation.definitionFit: To step down is to resign or withdraw from a post, to leave it.

clue.text: A fly was quiet

parts.note: a fly was a light hackney carriage pulled by a single animal, and a sleepy small town is described with the same adjective

explanation.definitionFit: A fly was a carriage drawn by a single horse; a small quiet place is a one-horse town.

clue.text: Written like an old movie

explanation.surface: Something in writing compared to a vintage film.
explanation.definitionFit: Printed text is black ink on white paper, the idiom for put in writing; early films were monochrome, without colour.

clue.text: The sort of dome thar's stuffed with religious belief

indicators.note: one thing filled with another, so the second word goes inside the first

parts.note: an onion dome is the bulbous roof of Russian churches
pi is slang for pious or religious

explanation.surface: Describing an onion-domed church packed with fervent faith.
explanation.walkthrough: An onion dome is the bulb-shaped cupola on Orthodox churches.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or conviction one holds, close to a belief.

clue.text: Drawn 18.demanding overturn of draw

parts.note: 18 across is a witch, and a hag is another word for a witch

indicators.note: overturned means the word for draw is turned back to front

parts.note: draw, as in pull, means drag

explanation.surface: A gaunt figure, the witch, demanding a tug be reversed.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' points to the answer of 18 across, a witch; 'overturn of' turns the word for draw back to front. 'Drawn' is the gaunt sense, not pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggard face looks gaunt and worn, as does a drawn one.

clue.text: Water above the average in quality

explanation.surface: Praising some water as better than usual.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Superior is one of the Great Lakes, a body of water; superior also means better than ordinary.

clue.text: Give a pupil knowledge appropriate to everyday life

parts.note: give knowledge, read together, means inform
L stands for learner, a pupil

explanation.surface: Teaching a student useful practical things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give' and 'knowledge' together make INFORM, with 'a pupil' (A L) placed after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal means casual, relaxed, suited to ordinary daily situations.

clue.text: French man and wife take part in recreation

parts.note: René is a common French man's name

explanation.surface: A Frenchman and his wife join in some leisure activity.
explanation.walkthrough: Recreation is read as re-creation: to renew is to create something again.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to restore or make afresh, taking part in a re-making.

clue.text: Live near Edinburgh, moving daughter out to make room for old

indicators.note: moving means the remaining letters are shifted around
one letter leaves so another can take its place

explanation.surface: A family living near Edinburgh rehouse a daughter to fit in an elderly relative.
explanation.walkthrough: D in EDINBURGH is replaced by O ('out to make room for'), then 'moving' rearranges EOINBURGH.
explanation.definitionFit: To neighbour a place is to be next to it, to live close by.

clue.text: Last act features one-time wife of Beery, W.

explanation.surface: A final performance featuring a former wife of a film actor.
explanation.walkthrough: Gloria Swanson was married to actor Wallace Beery; written like 'Beery, W.' her name is 'Swanson, G.'
explanation.definitionFit: A swansong is a final performance; Gloria Swanson, listed surname first, is Swanson G.

clue.text: Sycorax, perhaps, carrying around Caliban early on

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: carrying means with, as in a man with a bag

indicators.note: early on means just the first letter of Caliban

explanation.surface: Describing the mother in The Tempest holding her infant son.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's The Tempest Sycorax is the witch who is Caliban's mother. 'around' puts C ('early on' of Caliban) inside WITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycorax is the sorceress of The Tempest, an example of a sorceress or hag.

clue.text: It's very hard to get round island, very hard

indicators.note: to get round is to encircle, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: HH is the pencil grade for very hard lead
Ellis Island in New York Harbor

explanation.surface: Sailing around an island is a terribly tough task.
explanation.walkthrough: HH is the pencil grade for very hard; Ellis Island received US immigrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Hellish means extremely difficult or unpleasant.

clue.text: Being distracted, reinfect with disorder

indicators.note: disorder means the letters of reinfect are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: A patient, distracted, catches the same illness again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorder' rearranges REINFECT.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means frantic and agitated, the state of someone wildly distracted.

clue.text: Request partial translation of 'ventre à terre'

indicators.note: only part of the French phrase is carried over, hiding the answer in it

explanation.surface: Asking for a part translation of a French phrase meaning at full gallop.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside vENTRE A Terre; ventre à terre is French for flat out.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to beg or ask earnestly.

clue.text: Tree house

explanation.surface: A tree next to a house.
explanation.definitionFit: The citrus tree bears oranges; the House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty.

clue.text: By dubious means, he wins a billion 13 had invested

indicators.note: to invest is to put inside, so the letter goes into the word

parts.note: 13 across is superior, and nobler means superior

explanation.surface: A tale of a cheat winning by getting a rich backer to stake a billion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had invested' puts B inside NOBLER, a synonym of superior, the answer to 13 across.
explanation.definitionFit: A nobbler is someone who tampers with a racehorse or bribes a juror, winning unfairly.

clue.text: Set up centre to give advice about food

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the CAB is the Citizens Advice Bureau, a British free advice centre
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Opening an advice office about diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' reverses CAB, the Citizens Advice Bureau (a British free advice service).
explanation.definitionFit: Bacon is cured pork, a breakfast meat.

clue.text: He works in a diamond mine — he's in credit

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
he's gives the word he

explanation.surface: Describing a miner in a diamond mine who is well off.
explanation.walkthrough: The diamond is a baseball infield, not a jewel; the pitcher throws from its centre.
explanation.definitionFit: In baseball the pitcher throws the ball from the mound in the middle of the infield, called the diamond.

clue.text: Steps — purveyors of ladders know about their origins

indicators.note: their origins are the starting letters of the five preceding words

explanation.surface: Ladder sellers know about steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' suggests rungs, but it means dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively dance, its pattern of steps giving it its name.

clue.text: It's seldom Columbian gets involved with one twice

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up together
twice means the word one is used two times

explanation.surface: Something a Colombian rarely does: getting mixed up with a single person twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets involved' rearranges COLUMBIAN plus ONE ONE ('twice').
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something happening very rarely, almost never.

clue.text: Well-known Indian, the nominal producer of buffalo butter

definitions.text: the nominal producer of buffalo butter

explanation.surface: A famous Indian figure credited with making dairy fat.
explanation.walkthrough: Ghi (ghee) is Indian clarified butter, often from buffalo milk; the name read as G and HI produces those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement; his name split into G and HI spells ghi, the clarified butter.

clue.text: Some sin and end in the pit

parts.note: some means a part of something
to sin is to err

indicators.note: the end of the word the gives its last letter

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing that ends in the abyss.
explanation.walkthrough: The pit is the ground floor of a theatre, which is called the parterre.
explanation.definitionFit: A parterre is the area of a theatre behind the orchestra, known in Britain as the pit.
